EXAMPLE_TITLE_DEPRECATED_GETHTML: Deprecated rich text workaround with intl.getHTML
EXAMPLE_NOTE_PLAIN: Use ICU variables with the values passed to intl.get. Keep .d() as the default message and source text for extraction. See FormatJS ICU syntax for details.
EXAMPLE_NOTE_PLURAL: Plural messages use ICU plural rules. The # placeholder is formatted with the active locale, so large numbers get locale-aware separators. Learn more in the ICU MessageFormat guide.
EXAMPLE_NOTE_DATE_TIME: Pass JavaScript Date values and format them with ICU date/time styles such as short, medium, long, or full. See the intl-messageformat docs for supported formatting behavior.
EXAMPLE_NOTE_NUMBER_CURRENCY: Use ICU number formatting with a currency code such as USD. The rendered currency symbol, grouping, and decimal separators follow the active locale. See the intl-messageformat docs for more number formatting options.
EXAMPLE_NOTE_RICH_GET: Rich React components are supported in react-intl-universal@2.14+. Use get as the unified API for plain text, HTML-like markup, and React components.
EXAMPLE_NOTE_DEPRECATED_GETHTML: intl.getHTML is deprecated. Use get as the unified API for messages. To render rich React components with get, upgrade to react-intl-universal@2.14+. The getHTML examples below split one sentence into several messages, which is harder to translate correctly.
EXAMPLE_NOTE_SKILL: Start an AI coding request with $use-react-intl-universal when adding, reviewing, or migrating i18n code. The use-react-intl-universal skill helps keep messages extractable, grammatical, and consistent across locale files.
EXAMPLE_NOTE_EXTRACT: react-intl-universal-extract reads .d() default messages from source code and writes them into a locale JSON file. Keep .d() as the source text, then use the generated file as the base for translation.
